# Starter: semantic search round-trip

This is a small, standalone TypeScript project (not part of the Berkeleytime
monorepo) modeling a real data-flow shape from Berkeleytime's catalog search.

## Setup

```bash
cd starter
npm install
npm test          # run the test suite once
npm run test:watch  # rerun on file changes
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
```

## The task

`src/semanticSearch.ts` exports `semanticSearch(query)`. It's the entry point
for Berkeleytime's semantic (AI-ranked) catalog search: it asks an external
ranking service (`src/semanticSearchService.ts`, standing in for a real
Python microservice reached over HTTP) which classes best match a natural
language query, and needs to return those classes fully hydrated, in the
same order the ranking service returned them.

The function is currently a stub -- it throws `"not implemented"`. Your job
is to implement it, based on your Round 1 design (or a revised one, now that
you're looking at the concrete types and mocks). Read the JSDoc contract at
the top of `src/semanticSearch.ts` first -- it's the specification for what
a correct implementation must do. In short, it must:

1. Hydrate each ranked id from `catalogCache` (`src/catalogCache.ts`, a warm
   in-memory cache the ordinary non-semantic catalog search path already
   depends on) first.
2. Fall back to `dbLookup` (`src/dbLookup.ts`, standing in for a MongoDB
   round trip) only for ids that are a genuine cache miss, in a single
   batched call containing only the missing ids -- not the full ranked
   list, and not one call per miss.
3. Drop any id that resolves in neither the cache nor the "database"
   (a stale ranking-service entry) instead of throwing or returning a hole.
4. Preserve the ranking service's original order in the final result.

Read the comments at the top of `src/catalogCache.ts` and `src/dbLookup.ts`
too -- they spell out the exact fixture cases the tests check for, including
one deliberate cache-miss case. An implementation that never calls
`dbLookup` at all is wrong -- one of the fixtures depends on that fallback
path actually working. `dbLookup.ts` is instrumented with a call counter
and call-args log (`getDbLookupCallCount()` / `getDbLookupCallArgs()`)
specifically so the test suite can check both correctness of the returned
data and that the lookup is invoked as rarely and as narrowly as possible.

Run `npm test` to see the full suite fail against the stub. Do not edit the
test file, the fixtures, or the instrumentation helpers in `dbLookup.ts`; if
you think a test is wrong, say so in your writeup instead of changing it.

This should take a competent engineer roughly 1-2 hours of the 3-4 hour
slot, including using whatever AI tools you'd normally use. The remaining
time is for the code review discussion.

## AI tool usage

Use AI tools however you normally would for this kind of task. Please keep a
plain-text or markdown log of the prompts you used (a running log is fine --
doesn't need to be polished) and bring it to the code review. We're
interested in how you used the tool, what you kept vs. rejected, and where
you double-checked its output, not whether you used one at all.
